questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Vigilant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Negligent.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• “**Vigilant**” means** “to remain aware or to keep a watch on something or someone**.” (जागरूक, चौकन्ना)

 
 
• **Example: ***The guards were quite vigilant during the night, which prevented any sort of robbery in the locality.*
 
 
 
• “**Negligent**” refers to the **act of negligence or ignoring.(**सुस्त, असावधान**)**
 
 
• **Example**: *The guard had been negligent in their duty* for some days, which resulted in the robbery of the shop.
 
 
 
• Therefore, “**Negligent” **is the correct antonym for “**vigilant”**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**The meaning and usage of the other words are as follows:

 
• “**Stagnant**” means **stuck or sluggish. (**स्थिर)

 
 
• **Example**: *You should drain the stagnant water from that hole, or it would be a breeding ground for the mosquitos.*
 
 
 
• “**Robust”** means **strong. (**मज़बूत)
 
 
• **Example:** *He was struck by a robust sensation of joy after watching India wining the World Cup.*
 
 
 
• “**Dubious**” means **hesitating or doubting something.(**संदिग्ध)
 
 
• **Example**: *I cannot but be dubious about his method of working.*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The professor said, “I want you to pursue your dreams”

options.text: The professor said that I want you to pursue your dreams.
The professor said that he wanted me to pursue my dreams.

questions.solution:

• As the **sentence is in the past tense**, the **indirect sentence too will be in past tense.**
 
• **Option 1 and Option 3 **is incorrect as they are grammatically wrong.
 
• According to the rules of narration change **the reported speech** (the sentence within the quotation marks) **must follow the tense of the reported verb** (Main verb in the main cluse), here past tense.

• The pronoun in the **reported speech should be changed according to the subject and object of the main clause**.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

She has learned many lessons in this camp.

options.text: Many lessons has been learned by her in this camp.
Many lessons are being learned by her in this camp.
Many lessons have been learned by her in this camp.
Many lessons were learned by her in this camp.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Many lessons have been learned by her in this camp.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**In order to convert an active sentence into passive one-

__
 
• The **object **should be **converted into subject **and **the subject into an object.**
 
• A “**be”** verb should be added according to the tense and subject.
 
• As the sentence here is in** Present Perfect tense, **in the passive voice "**been**" should be used.
 
• The subject, “**She” ** will be “**her” **as the object, and a “**by” **will be added before it.
 
• “**Many Lessons”** will come to the subject position in the passive voice.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Many lessons have been learned by her in this camp.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 **is **incorrect** as the sentence is **grammatically incorrect** as the subject is in **plural form**; therefore it should be followed by “**have”.**
 
• **Option 2 **is **incorrect** as the sentence is in the **present continuous tense.**
 
• **Option 3 **is **incorrect** as the sentence is in the **past tense.**

questions.question:

__No sooner did this idea enter__ his head, than it carried conviction with it.

options.text: No sooner does this idea enter
No sooner do his idea enter
No sooner has his idea enter

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **No substitution.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• Using the **other options as substitution** would render the sentence **grammatically incorrect and meaningless**.
 
• The phrase **“no sooner”** is always followed by the verb “**did” or “had”. **

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

Holi is a festival of revelry and camaraderie which is __celebrated between the country__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **celebrated across the country.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **“Between” **is used as a preposition when there are two things.

 
 
• **Example: ***The chocolate should be divided between two brothers equally.*
 
 
 
• **“Across” **means from **one side to another side.**
 
 
• **Example: ***There is a wooden bridge across the river.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, **“celebrated between the country” **should be substituted with “**celebrated across the country”.**
 
• The correct sentence should be, **Holi is a festival of revelry and camaraderie which is celebrated *across* the country.**
 
• The rest of the options are incorrect; especially, options two and three are grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

The article that she wrote/for the last week's Sunday Supplement/fairly criticises/the abuse of mobile phones.

options.text: for the last week’s Sunday Supplement

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (4) **i.e. '**fairly criticises'.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is in the past form, which is denoted by the verb **“wrote”.**
 
• **'criticises' **should be written in the past form as **'criticised/criticized'.**
 
• In this context, it is said that An article was written on the abuse of mobile phones which was fairly criticised/criticized. It was published in the last week's Sunday Supplement.
 
• The rest of the parts of the sentence are correct as they follow the subject-verb agreement and the grammar.

Therefore, the correct sentence will be, The article that she wrote for the last week’s Sunday Supplement fairly *criticised/criticized* the abuse of mobile phones.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Play it by ear

options.text: To do something without special preparation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **to do something without special preparation.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Idiom refers to **a group of words or a phrase** whose meaning is **different from the normal syntactical meaning** of the phrase.
 
• "Play it by ear" is an idiom that means to make decision based on the situation as it is unfolding, rather than planning everything ahead of time.**. **
 
 
• **Example:** *As far as the game is concerned, we have to play it by ear for the first thirty minutes until the real captain arrives on the field.​*
 
 

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

Some other examples of idioms with the word “**ear**” include the following:

 
• “**All ears**” means “**to listen attentively**.”

 
 
• **Example:** *Tell me in detail about yesterday’s accident, I am all ears.*
 
 
 
• “**To lend an ear**” means “**to listen carefully and sympathetically**”.
 
 
• **Example**: *The best person to talk about this is Shyam, as he is always ready to lend an ear.*

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

Mother said that/it was quite all right/for her to get upset/for scoring less.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"it was quite all right".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The use of 'quite' in this context is superfluous.
 
• The adverb, 'quite' means not very. The use of 'quite' in this context is not necessary to emphasize the fact that the mother stated it was completely acceptable for her to become upset due to her lower score.
 
• Hence, 'quite' must be removed to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: *Mother said that it was all right for her to get upset for scoring less.*

S. The weather was ominous and it was raining too.

• I was in **west Bhutan**, on the **Chele La mountain crossing**. It was **raining and the sky was gloomy**. Yet, to attempt and gain a better look, my guide **Raj Lama** had me **hiking up yet another trail**. I told him I wasn't **impressed with him**.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The snow-storm might have delayed Mira.

options.text: Mira might have been delayed by the snow-storm.
Mira may be delayed by the snow-storm.
Mira might be delayed by the snow-storm.
Mira may have been delayed by the snow-storm.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Mira might have been delayed by the snow-storm."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When **a verb** acts on the **sentence's subject,** it is said to be in the **passive voice**.
 
• The given sentence is in the **present perfect** tense and we need to make **it in passive voice**.
 
• **Rule of passive voice** for present perfect tense: Object+**has/have+been+past participle form**+subject.

**Correct sentence:** Mira might have been delayed by the snow-storm.
